status: HELICOPTER AI HULL COMBAT CHECKPOINT PASSED; complete military/creature goal remains active
problem: AI fire rejected every first mechanical hull and required a LivingEntity first hit. Infected enemies in native tanks and helicopters could be tracked without their vehicle being fired upon.
implementation: Aim and last observation resolve the actual root vehicle body for native ground vehicles and helicopters. On-foot targets retain their original path.
Ground contacts use actual oriented hull geometry. Conservative hull AABBs and seated bodies are excluded from the ordinary entity ray so they cannot supersede the real hull surface.
AI permits its selected enemy carrier only with legitimate hostile occupants, rejecting empty, allied or mixed-friendly hulls. Rocket preflight also checks nearby friendly aircraft.
Machine gun uses existing mechanical armor factors. Rocket uses the actual native VehicleOrdnanceProjectile, finite stores and native collision/impact events.

Seated helicopter occupants are excluded from vehicle projectile direct and splash damage. Aircraft damage uses actual crew allegiance/creative/PvP rules instead of treating any remembered player owner as an enemy.
Direct aircraft projectile contact receives full configured direct damage once and is omitted from the same blast pass. This fixes incidental edge falloff and avoids double counting.
limitations: Existing machine gun and unguided rocket are Minecraft weapon profiles. Full original Hellfire/gun-pod/rocket selection, guidance, exact damage, timing and motion are not completed by this checkpoint.

Vehicle-target attack scenarios use infected enemy occupants. Radio-designated noninfected opponents need additional coverage: shared hull impact permission currently checks infection or the actual firing soldier target, while the aircraft keeps a separate designation.
Moving target interception, complex mixed traffic, multiplayer sessions, and new rendered/client sound review remain outside this server checkpoint.
Original FIG still contains opaque condition/track types; the source report lists them explicitly. No complete Apache-engine reconstruction is claimed.
qaIncident: An initial combined 68-test process exceeded the 1 GB game heap. NeoForge even returned Gradle success after the server OOM; that run is rejected. Logs preserved under combined-oom. Final runs split 39 helicopter and 29 shared-vehicle scenarios, and separate the 8 firing tests from the 13 basic vehicle tests into another batch without removing any cases.
